subject: AcmeBank: data residency & region pinning follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Williams <john.williams@acmebank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeBank discovery - data residency & region pinning

Hi John / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned before a technical deep dive: 

- Your core ask: ensure customer data (particularly PII) remains within the customer's geographic jurisdiction (EU customers in EU, US customers in US, APAC customers in APAC) while keeping options for predictable failover/DR.
- Retention: you mentioned a 7-year retention window for certain PII fields and shorter retention for application logs.
- Logging/audit: your security team needs to see access logs and audit trails and may request log exports to customer-managed storage.
- Encryption/KMS: customer-managed keys preferred for backups and long-term storage.
- Contracting: you flagged DPA language and SOC 2 evidence.

A few clarifying questions so we can prep the right folks for the deep dive: 
1) For region pinning, do you need strict enforcement (no cross-region movement under any circumstance) or is intra-boundary (e.g., EU->EU) fallback acceptable during platform-level failover?
2) For backups, do you require backups to be stored exclusively in-region, or is cross-region replica acceptable if encrypted & KMS-controlled?
3) Any specific retention windows for logs/metrics vs. PII? (You mentioned ~7 years for PII; what about audit logs?)

Next steps: I’ll loop in Aditya (cc’d) to provide technical details on our region pinning and failover modes. If it works, can we schedule a 60-min tech + security deep dive with your security team later this week? I’ll attach our SOC 2 overview and a short data residency whitepaper for reference.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-soc2-2025.pdf (SOC 2 summary), data-residency-whitepaper.pdf (short explainer)

Subject: Re: AcmeBank discovery - data residency & region pinning

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Regions: We need EU data for EU customers to remain in the EU for normal operations. Same for US and APAC (Singapore). In general, strict in-region storage is the requirement, but we can discuss limited cross-region failover only for declared DR events (and ideally only to another region within the same compliance boundary).
- Failover behaviour: Preferred approach is active-passive with manual DR failover; automatic cross-region failover is acceptable only with explicit agreement and auditability.
- Backups: Backups should by default be retained in-region for 30 days; longer-term retention for PII (up to 7 years) needs to be separately addressed (we may require exportable snapshots for long-term archival under strict controls).
- Logs: Audit logs for access/administration should be retained for 1 year. We may request a periodic export to our S3.
- DPA/SOC2: Please send SOC 2 evidence and a DPA template — we’ll circulate with legal. I’ve attached an initial DPA draft for your review (acme-dpa-draft.docx).

Yes — please put Aditya and your infra folks on a call with our security team. Times later this week or early next week work.

Best,
John Williams
Head of Cloud Security | AcmeBank
john.williams@acmebank.com

Attachment: acme-dpa-draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeBank discovery - data residency & region pinning

Thanks John — that helps a lot. Quick responses inline: 

- Regions / pinning: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning at the route level. You can pin workloads to a single region (strict mode) or a compliance-boundary group (e.g., any EU region) depending on your needs. By default we try to avoid cross-region data movement; automatic cross-region failover is off in "strict region" mode.
- Failover: We offer two modes: 
  * Strict region mode — no automatic cross-region failover; manual DR required to move traffic or data.
  * Regional-fallback mode — automatic failover to a configured regional sibling (e.g., EU-west -> EU-central) within the same compliance boundary.
- Backups & retention: Nightly snapshots are available. Default retention is 30 days; we support configurable retention policies up to 90 days and can export long-term snapshots to a customer-managed archive (encrypted with customer KMS).
- Logs/audit: Audit logs can be exported to customer S3 (or GCS) on a schedule; we retain control-plane logs per your retention policy but can provide a stream for your SIEM.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for backups and long-term storage.
- PII deletion: We expose API calls for targeted deletion and a compliance workflow to prove deletion.

I’ve attached the SOC 2 summary and a short data residency whitepaper for your legal/security review. Aditya — can you provide the specific config flags and the expected RTO/RPO for the regional-fallback vs strict-mode options so we can answer John’s DR question on the call?

Proposed next step: 60-min tech + security deep dive with your security team. Suggested times: Thu 3/26 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 3/27 09:00-10:00 PT. What works for your team?

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-soc2-2025.pdf, data-residency-whitepaper.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeBank discovery - data residency & region pinning - technical details

Hi John / Priya —

Following up with the technical specifics Marissa requested. TL;DR: region pinning is per-route/model, strict-mode prevents automatic cross-region read/write, and backups/replication are configurable to meet in-region-only requirements. Details below: 

1) Region pinning and routing
- Pinning level: per-customer or per-route (you can pin sensitive routes that touch PII while leaving non-sensitive routes distributed).
- Enforcement: edge-routing enforces locality; in strict-mode we reject traffic that would require data to move out of the pinned region and surface an error to the client.

2) Failover modes and RTO/RPO
- Strict-region mode: RTO depends on manual failover steps (we estimate 1-4 hours depending on orchestration); RPO is within the last snapshot (default snapshot cadence is hourly for high-availability workloads). No automatic cross-region promotion.
- Regional-fallback mode: automatic failover to a pre-configured sibling region within the same compliance boundary. RTO ~ 5-15 minutes (route switchover + KV cache warmup); RPO: last 1-2 minutes if using continuous replication on active-active variants; otherwise snapshot-based replication yields RPO = snapshot cadence.

3) Backups & long-term archival
- Snapshots: nightly and on-demand snapshots. By default snapshots are stored in-region.
- Cross-region replication: available as an opt-in feature; we will only replicate if explicitly configured and only to approved targets. Replicated snapshots are encrypted with customer-managed KMS if you enable CMK.
- Retention: configurable per-snapshot policy; default 30 days, configurable up to 90 days in the UI; for longer-term archiving we can push snapshots to your long-term archive (cold storage) with separate retention controls.

4) Logging, audit, and PII handling
- Audit logs: control-plane audit logs are retained per your policy and can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket. Access logs/response bodies: we offer an option to redact or disable response logging for sensitive routes.
- PII deletion: we support targeted deletion APIs, purge workflows, and tamper-evident deletion proofs for compliance.
- Encryption: TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys supported for disk and backup encryption.

5) Evidence / docs
- We attached the SOC 2 summary in the earlier email and a data residency whitepaper. If you need the full SOC 2 report or a signed DPA, Marissa can coordinate with our legal team.

Next steps: 
- Schedule the 60-min tech + security deep dive (Marissa proposed Thu/Fri). Please confirm availability and we’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.
- If helpful, we can prepare a short demo showing strict-mode vs regional-fallback in our staging environment.

Thanks —

Staff SWE, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
